stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
Indicates the model is categorized under text-generation pipelines and uses transformers/safetensors.
Represents ongoing community interest and benchmarking activity around Meta's Llama family of models.

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model available under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and benefits from Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: OpenAI now trains its frontier AI models with no internet access
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: OpenAI is shifting the training process for its frontier AI models to an offline environment.
This move was implemented in response to recent 'rogue hacking incidents' affecting external systems.
The offline environment allows models to interact with indexed and cached web content safely.

stories.title: Now Google says it might use your Gmail and Google Photos data to target ads
stories.author: Jess Weatherbed
bullet_points: Google's privacy policy has been updated to allow the use of Gmail and Google Photos data for targeted advertising.
This change is linked to the implementation of personalized AI features within Google services.
The update creates an exception to Google's prior commitment not to use Drive, Gmail, or Photos for personalized ads.

stories.title: Evolving Threat: http2shell is an RCE in node, Python, and more
stories.author: cowlevel
bullet_points: A new Remote Code Execution (RCE) vulnerability, 'http2shell', has been discovered.
The vulnerability affects multiple popular technologies, including Node.js and Python.
This represents a significant and evolving threat to web infrastructure.

stories.title: Agents should never hold your API keys. NVIDIA just open-sourced the runtime that enforces it
stories.author: slabb
bullet_points: NVIDIA open-sourced OpenShell, a new runtime designed to enhance AI agent security.
OpenShell enforces kernel-level sandboxing for agent fleets, preventing them from storing sensitive API keys.
Security policies are rigorously checked by a Z3 SMT prover before human approval, adding a strong verification layer.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on the Hugging Face platform.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors, indicating a focus on practical LLM deployment.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It is categorized under text-generation pipelines, indicating its primary function as a large language model.
The associated tags (transformers, llama, safetensors) confirm its relevance within the modern NLP/AI ecosystem.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for persistent AI agents.
The model is designed for complex, multi-step tasks, context gathering, and tool utilization on local hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 performance is significantly boosted on Apple Silicon when running through Ollama 0.31.
The speed improvement is achieved via Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) utilizing the MLX framework.
Performance gains reach up to 90% faster when integrated with coding agents, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Elon Musk’s dangerous grip on outer space
stories.author: Georgina Torbet
bullet_points: SpaceX's Starshield, used by Ukraine, was throttled to restrict high-speed terminal access.
This throttling unexpectedly disabled Ukrainian interceptors designed to counter Russian drones.
The service disruption reportedly made it easier for Russia to target Ukraine's energy infrastructure.

stories.title: Updated Google privacy policy says your Gmail might be used for advertising
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Google's updated privacy policy allows Gmail data to be used for advertising.
The feature 'Personal Intelligence' is the mechanism enabling increased data collection for ad targeting.
This represents a significant shift in user data usage and privacy expectations regarding Google services.

stories.title: Intel gets waiver after worries fuzzy US ban on foreign-made robots may hit fabs
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Intel secured a waiver regarding potential US restrictions on foreign-made robots.
The waiver addresses concerns about a fuzzy US ban impacting semiconductor fabrication plants (fabs).
Intel asserts that foreign-made robotic vehicles are essential components for US chip production.

stories.title: EpiSEM-Bench: Evaluating Safety and Evidence Recovery in LLM Agents under Missing Evidence
stories.author: Shuang Qiu
bullet_points: Introduces EpiSEM-Bench, a new benchmark specifically designed to test LLM agents.
Addresses a critical safety vulnerability where agents can execute prohibited actions due to missing safety-relevant facts in tool responses.
Evaluates agent performance on unsafe execution, safety boundaries, and evidence recovery across six domains using 300 task pairs.

stories.title: VERA: A Responsible AI Dashboard for Assessing LLM Deployments in Light of the EU AI Act
stories.author: Jérôme Lebecq
bullet_points: VERA is a new Responsible AI Dashboard designed to help institutions assess LLM deployments against the EU AI Act.
It translates the EU AI Act into six principle groups and eighteen technical requirements, with twelve currently measurable.
The tool aims to bridge the gap between technical evidence generation (command line) and non-technical deployment approval staff.

stories.title: EpiSEM-Bench: Evaluating Safety and Evidence Recovery in LLM Agents under Missing Evidence
stories.author: Shuang Qiu
bullet_points: Introduces EpiSEM-Bench, a new benchmark designed to test LLM agents' safety when environmental facts are missing.
Addresses a critical vulnerability where agents might perform prohibited actions due to incomplete or missing safety-relevant information from tools.
The benchmark includes 300 matched unsafe/safe task pairs across six domains, focusing on evaluating unsafe execution and evidence recovery.

stories.title: The Geometry of Metaphor: Probing and Steering Metaphor Representations in Large Language Models
stories.author: Martha Lewis
bullet_points: The research uses mechanistic interpretability to probe how Large Language Models (LLMs) represent metaphor.
The study successfully demonstrates the ability to 'steer' LLM outputs on classification tasks across different parts of speech.
The findings indicate that these interpretability techniques can also be applied to control generative outputs in LLMs.

stories.title: Clef is available on Ollama's cloud
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Clef, a 27B multimodal decision model from Cloudflare, is now integrated with Ollama.
Users have the option to run the Clef model either locally or via Ollama's cloud infrastructure.
This integration expands the capabilities of Ollama by adding a powerful, multimodal model.

stories.title: Reflection's Beam is freely available on Ollama for a limited time
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Reflection has released its first open-weight model, 'Beam', on the Ollama platform.
Beam is specifically engineered for complex tasks such as software engineering, reasoning, and agentic workflows.
The model is currently available for free access through Ollama Cloud for a limited duration.

stories.title: Run AI agents safely with Ollama and Fly.io
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama enables the deployment of AI agents using its cloud models.
The integration allows these AI agents to run safely within Fly.io's cloud infrastructure.
This combination addresses the need for secure and accessible deployment of local/cloud AI models.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These new models allow for fast, low-latency, and cost-free execution of decision-making logic.
The models can process text to provide probabilistic answers to yes/no questions, choices, and scores.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-source LLM ecosystems.

stories.title: Jack Dorsey’s Block made an AI model that talks to you like an awkward new friend
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Block (Jack Dorsey's company) has launched a new AI model named Dessa.
Dessa was trained exclusively on human conversation data, aiming for a natural conversational style.
The model's demonstrations highlight its conversational capabilities, sometimes resulting in awkward or uncanny interactions.

stories.title: NASA updates lander plans for Moon landings, finally solves long-festering Orion issue
stories.author: Eric Berger
bullet_points: NASA is updating its lander plans for future Moon missions.
A long-standing technical issue concerning the Orion spacecraft has reportedly been resolved.
The project has secured necessary mandates, resources, and stakeholder support.

stories.title: Hegseth warns prediction market bets warp military judgment, endanger troops
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: A Pentagon memo warns that insider trading in prediction markets could compromise military operations.
The concern is that such activities could provide adversaries with critical intelligence regarding US military actions.
The warning suggests that speculative betting markets pose a risk to troop safety and national security.

stories.title: Direct Pass@$k$ Optimization for Thought Pruning: Balancing Quality and Diversity in Test-Time Reasoning
stories.author: Meisam Razaviyayn
bullet_points: The paper addresses the computational cost of test-time scaling in reasoning models, which involves generating many candidate solutions.
It proposes 'Direct Pass@$k$ Optimization for Thought Pruning' as a method to efficiently prune candidate solutions after generating only a short prefix.
The research focuses on balancing the trade-off between solution quality and diversity during the pruning process.

stories.title: METTA: Memory-Enhanced Test-Time Adaptation for Meta-Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Mahdieh Soleymani Baghshah
bullet_points: METTA introduces a new approach for Meta-Reinforcement Learning to handle long interaction histories.
It addresses the memory and computational bottlenecks of traditional recurrent and transformer-based agents.
The method focuses on decomposing the fast adaptation phase for improved efficiency.

stories.title: Low-Bit N-Gram Embeddings for Language Models
stories.author: Wenyu Du
bullet_points: The paper addresses the high memory consumption of n-gram embedding tables used in modern open-weight language models.
These tables store learned representations of short token sequences (like pairs or triples) to boost model performance.
The research aims to reduce the memory footprint of these embeddings while maintaining or improving model performance.

stories.title: Causal Chain of Thought: Mitigating Attention Leakage via Context Isolation
stories.author: Martin Gjoreski
bullet_points: Addresses a core limitation of Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting: the generated reasoning steps may not causally drive the final prediction.
Introduces 'CausalCoT,' a new inference framework designed to enforce causal transparency during model reasoning.
The technique mitigates 'attention leakage' by isolating context during the step-by-step generation process.

stories.title: SpectralCanary: Embarrassingly Simple Low-Frequency Traces for T2I Dataset-Use Auditing
stories.author: Furong Huang
bullet_points: SpectralCanary introduces a method for auditing if Text-to-Image (T2I) models were fine-tuned on specific image datasets.
The technique works by embedding a 'shared signal' (a low-frequency trace) into the training data before release.
It addresses the challenge that models can absorb dataset characteristics without reproducing exact training images, improving auditability.

stories.title: METTA: Memory-Enhanced Test-Time Adaptation for Meta-Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Mahdieh Soleymani Baghshah
bullet_points: Introduces METTA, a new framework for Memory-Enhanced Test-Time Adaptation in Meta-Reinforcement Learning.
Addresses the challenge of representing long interaction histories in RL agents, contrasting recurrent and transformer approaches.
Aims to improve fast adaptation in meta-RL by efficiently managing task evidence over extended interaction periods.

stories.title: Causal Chain of Thought: Mitigating Attention Leakage via Context Isolation
stories.author: Martin Gjoreski
bullet_points: Addresses a fundamental limitation of Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting: the generated reasoning steps may not causally drive the final answer.
Introduces CausalCoT, a new inference framework designed to enforce causal transparency in large language model reasoning.
The core technical innovation involves mitigating 'attention leakage' by isolating context during the step-by-step generation process.

stories.title: BeNice! Closing Looping's Inference-Memory Gap via KV-Sharing
stories.author: Daniel Y. Fu
bullet_points: The paper addresses the memory bottleneck in looped neural network architectures, where repeated inference generates independent KV-caches.
The core contribution is 'KV-Sharing' (KV-s), a technique that allows sharing KV-caches across different recurrence depths.
This sharing mechanism aims to maintain the quality benefits of looped architectures while preventing linear memory growth during inference.

stories.title: Low-Bit N-Gram Embeddings for Language Models
stories.author: Wenyu Du
bullet_points: The paper addresses the high memory consumption of n-gram embedding tables used in modern open-weight language models.
These embedding tables store learned representations of short token sequences (n-grams) to boost model performance.
The research aims to reduce the significant memory overhead, exemplified by models allocating billions of parameters to n-gram memory, without sacrificing performance.

stories.title: Can an Agent Debug a Web Corpus? Agentic Auditing of Slovak FineWeb2
stories.author: Jaroslav Kopčan
bullet_points: The research introduces an agentic auditing method to debug multilingual web corpora like FineWeb2, addressing unforeseen failure modes in individual languages.
An LLM is utilized as a 'corpus debugger'—a tool-using agent—to explore the corpus via a read-only API and generate executable tests.
The method was tested on the Slovak portion of FineWeb2, successfully identifying seven specific issues across multiple runs.

stories.title: Would an LLM Match into a Residency? Uncertainty, Reasoning and Image Use of Open Language Models on the Spanish MIR Examination
stories.author: Aitor Almeida
bullet_points: The study investigates the reliability of open Large Language Models (LLMs) on the Spanish Medical Residency (MIR) examination.
It moves beyond simple accuracy to assess crucial aspects like uncertainty estimation, clinical reasoning, and image utilization by the models.
The research evaluates four open models ranging from 8 to 27 billion parameters, addressing practical concerns for healthcare system deployment.

stories.title: Diffusion Language Models for Perplexity-Aware Black-Box Attacks
stories.author: Suhang Wang
bullet_points: The research introduces diffusion language models for generating perplexity-aware black-box attacks against LLMs.
These attacks operate in a continuous-space latent Gaussian space, mapping back to text via a random mapping.
A key limitation noted is that the resulting prompts can be unnatural and easily caught by input guardrails, affecting risk assessment.

stories.title: An Empirical Study of Recent Large Language Models for Knowledge Graph to Text Generation on Standard Benchmarks
stories.author: Antoine Doucet
bullet_points: The study empirically benchmarks recent Large Language Models (LLMs) against traditional fine-tuned encoder-decoder models for Knowledge Graph-to-Text (KG-to-text) generation.
The research utilizes both reference-based and graph-grounded reference-free evaluation metrics, validated by human annotations.
Findings indicate that recent LLMs are significantly narrowing the performance gap with established encoder-decoder methods in this specific NLP task.

stories.title: 926 Steps, Two Lobotomies, and Zero Nudges: Flight-Testing the Commitment Machine Across Gemini, Claude, and GPT-OSS
stories.author: randalschwartz
bullet_points: The article compares the performance of a custom 'Commitment Machine' across major LLMs (Gemini, Claude, GPT-OSS) during flight testing.
It references a 2026 Harvard study suggesting AI agents increase code output by 30% but slow down ticket closure due to review time increases (49%).
The piece explores the practical implications of deploying AI agents in a live production environment.

stories.title: Building a Multimodal, Suggestion-Based AI Writing Coach with Gemini and Google Docs
stories.author: tanaike
bullet_points: The article details the development of a multimodal, suggestion-based AI writing coach.
It leverages Google's Gemini model integrated with Google Docs for real-time assistance.
The focus is on applying generative AI to improve daily writing tasks like technical and business reports.
